chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafsh ibn Suqah from whom he informed him, saying:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to his wife from behind her. He said: It is one of the two types of intercourse, and in it is the ritual bath (ghusl).
ai.seo_question: Does sexual intercourse from behind require ghusl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that sexual intercourse from behind is considered a valid form of vaginal penetration, thereby necessitating *Ghusl al-Janabah* (major ritual purification) just as in the anterior position. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh as it distinguishes between acts that require full purification versus those that do not, emphasizing the physical act of penetration rather than the specific posture or direction. The hadith is found in the chapter discussing intercourse 'other than the front,' highlighting the juristic focus on the nature of the union rather than aesthetic preferences.
